feature: Document draft branching — Merge/Rebase open the Compare dialog to review before applying

callouts.text: 1 · Click Drafts in the top-left shell, then New draft
2 · Rename Planner to "Planner v2" in the inspector — the bar's Compare count becomes 1
3 · Click Compare 1 Change. This stays a PURE review: no checkboxes, no confirm bar, nothing to press.

4 · Close it, then click Merge — ONE click, no arming. The SAME dialog reopens, titled "Merge changes", every changed element ticked, with "› Merge 1 change" at the bottom right. Untick Planner v2: the confirm greys out and says applying only some changes isn't supported yet.

5 · Re-tick it and close. Now click the chevron beside Merge, then Rebase. The right-hand board is captioned "<draft> (after Rebase)" — the draft as it WOULD look, computed before anything is applied. Confirming runs the real Rebase.

PASS WHEN · Compare opens with NO checkboxes and NO bottom bar · Merge and Rebase each open the same dialog with a per-element tick and one confirm · unticking anything disables the confirm and explains why instead of quietly applying everything · the Rebase review's after-board is the proposed draft, not Main · confirming Merge writes to Main and closes the dialog; a Main that moved underneath refuses IN the dialog and leaves both sides intact
